one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented a naive nested-loop C extension (lacking BLAS/LAPACK) and exhausted the trajectory in repeated low-level micro-optimization cycles (loop unrolling, OpenMP, compiler flags) that never closed the gap from ~1.1x to the required 1.2x speedup for N=5000 assets.
t_err_evidence: Agent implements C risk function with basic nested loops, no BLAS/optimized approach to achieve required speedup.
t_commit_evidence: Step 13: First benchmark run shows 1.1x speedup for N=5000 (requirement is 1.2x) and a hang at N=8000; the agent proceeds with micro-optimizations on the same nested-loop structure rather than reconsidering the algorithm, locking in the failing trajectory.
t_surface_evidence: Benchmark shows speedup 1.1x < 1.2x required; performance requirement NOT met.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked the domain/API knowledge that BLAS (e.g., cblas_dgemv from OpenBLAS/MKL) is the standard way to obtain the required speedup for dense matrix-vector multiplication in a C extension; instead it relied on manual loop unrolling and OpenMP which were insufficient to overcome Python interpreter overhead at the N=5000 scale.
